de34_repurposing.topic: Repurposing test: documented cases of immigration and foreign-affairs tools used against named critics (visas, sanctions), status as of Oct 2026

claims.text: Rumeysa Öztürk, a Turkish PhD student at Tufts, was arrested by immigration agents in Somerville in March 2025 after the State Department revoked her student visa; the only basis that emerged was an op-ed she co-authored in the student newspaper about the university's response to the war in Gaza; held 45 days in Louisiana; a federal judge in Vermont ordered her release in May 2025, finding a substantial claim of retaliation for speech; on 29 Jan 2026 an immigration judge terminated removal proceedings, finding DHS had not proved her removable

April 2026: Öztürk and the government settled; the administration dropped its pursuit of deportation and affirmed her lawful student status; she finished her PhD and returned to Turkey; joint motion to dismiss filed 17 Apr 2026, court retains jurisdiction to enforce

Mahmoud Khalil, a lawful permanent resident and recent Columbia graduate, was arrested 8 March 2025; an immigration judge found him removable on 11 April 2025 'solely on Marco Rubio's determination' that his advocacy harmed US foreign policy; Judge Farbiarz found the 'Rubio policy' likely unconstitutional (28 May 2025) and he was released in June 2025; in Sept 2025 an immigration judge ordered him deported over alleged omissions in his green-card application; on 15 Jan 2026 a 2-1 Third Circuit panel held the district court lacked jurisdiction; rehearing en banc denied 22 May 2026; mandate stayed 26 May 2026 pending a Supreme Court petition
DHS (McLaughlin) said Khalil should 'self-deport now'; the administration called the release order an 'unprecedented' intrusion into its enforcement authority

14 Oct 2025: the State Department revoked visas of six foreign nationals (from Argentina, South Africa, Mexico, Brazil, Germany, Paraguay) over social-media comments on Charlie Kirk's assassination: 'The United States has no obligation to host foreigners who wish death on Americans'

18 Aug 2025: a State Department official said more than 6,000 student visas had been revoked since Rubio took office, about 4,000 for violations of law (assault, DUI, burglary); about 200 to 300 for 'support for terrorism'; Rubio (March 2025): 'Every time I find one of these lunatics, I take away their visas'

June 2026: a D.C. Circuit per curiam order partially stayed the district court's preliminary injunction pending appeal, so sanctions on UN Special Rapporteur Francesca Albanese (imposed July 2025 under EO 14203, citing her calls for ICC warrants) are enforceable again; her assets frozen, US persons barred from dealing with her; a concurrence suggested her First Amendment argument may fail; case unresolved
Khalil is 'a legal permanent resident of the United States'; Rubio said his continued presence 'would have potentially serious adverse foreign policy consequences'
